status: Draft key points written for M4.5 Track E on 2026-10-09; Matthew reviews them before the first scored run counts.
rules: Each key point is one checkable statement that a good report on the question must convey. Wording need not match. 'source' names where a reviewer can confirm it, and is not given to the system under test.

questions.question: Does LoRA match full fine-tuning quality for large language models, and where does it fall short?

key_points.text: LoRA freezes the pretrained weights and trains low-rank (rank-decomposition) update matrices injected into the Transformer layers.
The original LoRA paper reports quality on par with or better than full fine-tuning on RoBERTa, DeBERTa, GPT-2 and GPT-3, with far fewer trainable parameters and no added inference latency.
Controlled comparisons on programming and mathematics find LoRA substantially underperforms full fine-tuning in standard low-rank settings, especially for continued pretraining.
LoRA forgets less: it better preserves the base model's performance outside the target domain than full fine-tuning.
QLoRA fine-tunes LoRA adapters on a frozen 4-bit quantized base model, making 65B-parameter fine-tuning fit on a single 48 GB GPU.

questions.question: What is FlashAttention and why is it faster than standard attention?

key_points.text: FlashAttention computes exact attention (not an approximation).
It is IO-aware: it tiles the computation so blocks stay in on-chip SRAM, reducing reads and writes to GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which dominate runtime.
It never materialises the full N x N attention matrix; the backward pass recomputes attention from saved softmax statistics, so memory grows linearly with sequence length.
FlashAttention-2 improves parallelism and work partitioning for roughly a 2x speedup over the first version; FlashAttention-3 targets Hopper GPUs with asynchrony and FP8.

questions.question: How do mixture-of-experts language models reduce compute per token, and what makes them hard to train and serve?

key_points.text: A router sends each token to only the top-k experts (k=1 in Switch Transformer, k=2 in Mixtral), so active parameters per token are far fewer than total parameters.
key_points.source: Fedus et al. 2021, arXiv:2101.03961; Jiang et al. 2024, arXiv:2401.04088

key_points.text: An auxiliary load-balancing loss (or an equivalent mechanism) is needed to stop routing from collapsing onto a few experts.
key_points.source: Shazeer et al. 2017, arXiv:1701.06538; Fedus et al. 2021

key_points.text: Training can be unstable; remedies include the router z-loss and capacity factors with token dropping.
Serving needs memory for all experts, so memory scales with total parameters, not active ones (Mixtral 8x7B: about 47B total, about 13B active per token).

questions.question: What does the Chinchilla paper conclude about compute-optimal scaling of language models, and has it held up?

key_points.text: For a fixed compute budget, model size and training tokens should be scaled in roughly equal proportion.
Chinchilla (70B parameters, about 1.4T tokens) outperformed the much larger Gopher (280B) trained with the same compute.
This revises Kaplan et al. (2020), whose laws favoured growing model size faster than data.
The result is often summarised as roughly 20 training tokens per parameter.
key_points.source: Hoffmann et al. 2022 (Table 3); widely cited heuristic

key_points.text: A 2024 replication attempt found problems with one of the paper's three estimation approaches (the parametric fit), while the corrected estimate stays close to the other two.

questions.question: What are the trade-offs between SQLite's WAL mode and its rollback-journal mode?

key_points.text: In WAL mode readers do not block the writer and the writer does not block readers, but there is still only one writer at a time.
WAL is usually faster for writes, needing fewer fsyncs per transaction.
WAL relies on shared memory (the -shm wal-index), so every process must be on the same host; it does not work over a network filesystem.
Checkpoints copy WAL content back into the database; long-running readers can starve checkpoints and let the WAL file grow without bound.

questions.question: What does RFC 9309 specify about how crawlers must interpret robots.txt?

key_points.text: The most specific (longest) matching rule wins; when an allow and a disallow rule match equally, allow should be used.
If robots.txt is unavailable with a 4xx status the crawler may access any resource; if it is unreachable (5xx or network error) the crawler must assume complete disallow.
Crawlers must parse at least 500 kibibytes of the file.
Crawlers should not use a cached robots.txt for more than 24 hours, unless it is unreachable.
Rules support the '*' wildcard and the '$' end-of-path anchor; crawl-delay is not part of the standard.

questions.question: Which techniques most reduce LLM decoding latency on a single GPU, and why do they work?

key_points.text: Autoregressive decoding is memory-bandwidth bound: each token reads all the weights, so moving fewer bytes per token is what speeds it up.
key_points.source: e.g. Leviathan et al. 2023; Kim et al. 2023 (SqueezeLLM), arXiv:2306.07629

key_points.text: Speculative decoding has a small draft model propose several tokens that the target model verifies in one pass, giving the same output distribution as the target model.
key_points.source: Leviathan et al. 2023, arXiv:2211.17192; Chen et al. 2023, arXiv:2302.01318

key_points.text: Low-bit weight quantization (e.g. 4-bit GPTQ or AWQ) cuts the bytes read per token, and so cuts latency, at a small quality cost.
key_points.source: Frantar et al. 2022, arXiv:2210.17323; Lin et al. 2023, arXiv:2306.00978

key_points.text: The KV cache avoids recomputing attention over past tokens; PagedAttention (vLLM) manages it in blocks to cut fragmentation, which mainly raises throughput and batch size.

questions.question: What caused the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster in 1986?

key_points.text: An O-ring seal in a field joint of the right solid rocket booster failed, letting hot gas escape and leading to the break-up about 73 seconds after launch on 28 January 1986.
The unusually cold launch-day temperature reduced the O-rings' resilience.
Morton Thiokol engineers warned against launching in the cold, and the concern was overruled in the launch decision.
The Rogers Commission faulted NASA's decision-making and communication as well as the joint design; Richard Feynman showed O-ring stiffness in iced water.

questions.question: How do mRNA vaccines work, and what made them practical?

key_points.text: The mRNA encodes an antigen (for COVID-19 vaccines, the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein) that the body's cells translate, prompting an immune response.
key_points.source: e.g. Pardi et al. 2018, Nat Rev Drug Discov, doi:10.1038/nrd.2017.243

key_points.text: The mRNA is delivered inside lipid nanoparticles.
Modified nucleosides (pseudouridine, later N1-methylpseudouridine) reduce innate immune activation; Kariko and Weissman's work on this won the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
The mRNA does not enter the nucleus or change the recipient's DNA, and it is degraded naturally.
The first COVID-19 mRNA vaccines needed cold storage, ultra-cold (about -80 to -60 C) for Pfizer-BioNTech's original formulation.

questions.question: Does intermittent fasting produce more weight loss than ordinary daily calorie restriction?

key_points.text: When total calorie intake is matched, randomized trials generally find weight loss similar to daily calorie restriction, not superior.
A one-year trial of alternate-day fasting versus daily calorie restriction (Trepanowski et al., JAMA Internal Medicine 2017) found no superior weight loss or adherence for fasting.
A 12-month trial of time-restricted eating plus calorie restriction versus calorie restriction alone (Liu et al., NEJM 2022) found no significant difference in weight loss.
The TREAT trial (Lowe et al., JAMA Internal Medicine 2020) of 16:8 time-restricted eating found no significant weight-loss benefit over consistent meal timing.
The evidence is limited by short durations, small samples and adherence problems, so a claim of superiority should be reported as contested or unsupported.
key_points.source: reviewer judgement over the trials above
